sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Despite advances in the multimodal treatment of resectable esophagogastric adenocarcinoma (EGA), relapse rates remain high. No human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-targeted treatment is yet established in the perioperative setting. While trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) has compelling efficacy and is now a well-established drug in the treatment of advanced HER2-positive EGA, safety and efficacy data from the perioperative setting are still lacking.

sec.title: Methods
sec.p: NeoART is a phase Ib/II platform trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of neoadjuvant T-DXd-containing combination regimens for patients with HER2-positive EGA. We report about the safety, feasibility, and preliminary antitumor activity from the safety run-in cohort of the NeoART trial in which patients with locally advanced resectable EGA received three cycles of preoperative T-DXd (5.4 mg/kg, Q3W) combined with 5-fluorouracil (5-FU; 2,600 mg/m2 24 h, Q2W) and folinic acid (FA; 200 mg/m2, Q2W).

sec.title: Results
sec.p: In the preplanned safety analysis of the first 6 patients recruited to NeoART, no serious adverse events (SAEs) or dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) were reported during neoadjuvant treatment. Relevant treatment-related adverse events of grades 1–3 were diarrhea, mucositis, and nausea, but none fulfilled the criteria of DLTs. No relevant hematologic toxicity was observed. Five of six patients underwent curative-intent oncologic resection. In one patient, peritoneal carcinomatosis was detected at the time of surgery; therefore, the tumor was not resected. Two patients experienced grade 3 postoperative complications according to Clavien-Dindo classification, including one anastomotic leakage which was classified as an SAE. R0 resection was accomplished in four out of five resected patients. Histopathological complete remission (pCR; ypT0 N0) was observed in two patients.

sec.title: Conclusions
sec.p: Neoadjuvant treatment with T-DXd plus 5-FU/FA was found to be well tolerated and showed preliminary signs of activity during the safety run-in period of the NeoART study.
Keywords: Esophagogastric adenocarcinoma, Neoadjuvant treatment, Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2, Trastuzumab deruxtecan, Safety
Received 2026 Mar 2; Accepted 2026 Apr 29.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Esophagogastric adenocarcinoma (EGA) has a global incidence rate of 9.2/100,000 [1]. Despite advances in the multimodal treatment of resectable EGA, relapse rates remain high in the locally advanced stages [2, 3]. Recently, perioperative durvalumab in combination with chemotherapy (ctx) has shown improved event-free and overall survival in biomarker-unselected patients with resectable EGA [4, 5]. However, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-targeted perioperative therapy has not yet been established as a treatment for resectable EGA. While the combination of HER2-targeted antibodies and neoadjuvant ctx with or without programmed cell death 1 inhibition has been associated with high histopathological response rates, a survival benefit has not yet been demonstrated [6–8]. Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), a HER2-targeting antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), has demonstrated superior efficacy in second- and third-line treatment of metastatic HER2-positive EGA compared to conventional ctx, and high response rates were reported when T-DXd was combined with ctx in the first-line setting [9–11]. We designed a trial to assess the safety and feasibility of T-DXd plus ctx in the perioperative setting for patients with resectable HER2-positive EGA in the western hemisphere.

sec.title: Study Design and Treatment Regimens
sec.p: UCCL-IKF-AIO-STO-0124 NeoART is an international, open-label, non-randomized phase Ib/II trial evaluating safety and feasibility of T-DXd in combination with different ctx regimens. The trial is conducted within the Arbeitsgemeinschaft Internistische Onkologie (AIO) of the German Cancer Society, is registered at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT06731803), and will be expanded to centers in Austria and the Czech Republic. The design and protocol of the NeoART trial have been previously published [12]. Briefly, patients with histologically confirmed HER2-positive, locally advanced, resectable EGA (cT2–4, any cN, M0, or any cT, cN+, M0) receive neoadjuvant T-DXd combined with 5-fluorouracil (5-FU)/folinic acid (FA) or, planned for a later cohort, combined with 5-FU/FA and oxaliplatin. Disease assessment is performed with contrast-enhanced CT or MRI of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis, with additional imaging as clinically indicated. Diagnostic laparoscopy is required to exclude peritoneal carcinomatosis in patients with T3/T4 gastric tumors and in type II/III adenocarcinomas of the esophagogastric junction (AEG) according to Siewert classification, in line with guidelines. T and N stage is additionally assessed by endoluminal ultrasound. The NeoArt protocol does not define biopsy procedures; participating centers follow established routines and guideline recommendations. For the preplanned safety analysis, we evaluated the AEs, feasibility, and preliminary antitumor activity in the first six patients – the safety run-in of cohort 001 – treated with T-DXd (5.4 mg/kg, Q3W) plus 5-FU 2,600 mg/m2 over 24 h, Q2W, and FA (200 mg/m2, Q2W).

sec.title: Safety Analysis
sec.p: A preplanned safety analysis was foreseen after the first six recruited patients completed neoadjuvant treatment after which the study recruitment was interrupted until safety and feasibility were analyzed. The investigational regimen was considered not feasible if DLT occurred in more than 1 out of 6 patients. This corresponds to an acceptability threshold of approximately 17% (1 in 6) and an unacceptability threshold of about 33% (more than 1 in 3). Accordingly, a desirable feasibility rate was defined as 83% or higher (i.e., 100%–17%). Table 1 summarizes the predefined DLTs.

(b) Study treatment-related grade ≥4 AEs of any etiology

(c) Any study treatment-related AEs leading to the premature withdrawal of protocol treatment (excluding discontinuation of individual substances due to prior unknown allergy or hypersensitivity to these study drugs)

fn.p: Dose delays/interruptions of up to 10 days, which are not due to treatment-related grade ≥3 non-hematological AEs or treatment-related grade ≥4 AEs of any etiology are acceptable and will not be considered as failure.
AE, adverse event; DLTs, dose-limiting toxicities.

sec.p: AEs were defined according to the International Conference on Harmonization Guideline for Good Clinical Practice [13] and the Common Terminology Criteria (CTC) for AEs of the National Cancer Institute [14]. Perioperative morbidity and mortality are reported according to the Clavien-Dindo classification [15].

sec.title: Efficacy Analysis
sec.p: The pCR (ypT0 N0) by local assessment and the R0 resection rate are reported as secondary endpoints. R0 resection was defined as complete tumor removal with negative margins, while R1 resection indicated microscopic residual tumor. Tumor response is reported as tumor regression grade (TRG) according to Becker: 1a = no residual tumor in tumor bed (is equivalent to ypT0); 1b = <10% residual tumor in tumor bed; 2 = 10–50% residual tumor in tumor bed; and 3 = >50% residual tumor in tumor bed [16]. The absence of viable tumor cells in both the primary tumor and the resected lymph nodes (ypT0 N0) was defined as pCR.

sec.title: Patient Characteristics and Treatment for the Safety Run-In Cohort 001
sec.p: From April to July 2025, 6 patients were enrolled at six German sites. All patients completed the planned three cycles of T-DXd plus four cycles of 5-FU/FA. Table 2 summarizes patient demographics and tumor characteristics. Oncological resections, defined as the appropriate radical removal of the primary tumor and lymphadenectomy according to guideline recommendations, depending on tumor location and histological subtype (e.g., Ivor Lewis procedure for AEG type I), had been performed in five of six patients. In one patient, imaging at restaging – but not at baseline staging – indicated peritoneal carcinomatosis, which was confirmed by diagnostic laparoscopy; consequently, no resection was undertaken. Because of the tumor location in the esophagus (AEG type I), pretherapeutic staging laparoscopy had not been performed. Of note, in the five resected patients, the pretherapeutic biomarker assessment showed a HER2 3+ status by immunohistochemistry (IHC), while in the non-resected patient, HER2 status was only 2+ IHC and in situ hybridization was borderline positive with a ratio of 2.3. Further genetic analyses have not been performed. Table 3 summarizes the biomarker status of all the 6 patients. For the CONSORT checklist, please refer to the online supplementary material (for all online suppl. material, see https://doi.org/10.1159/000552693).

sec.title: Safety Results
sec.p: All 6 patients experienced at least one AE, mostly CTC grade 1. Two of the 6 patients had one AE of grade 2. However, according to the investigator’s and sponsor’s assessment, those were not classified as being treatment-related. One patient had grade 3 diarrhea which resolved within 72 h with loperamide as needed and does therefore not qualify as DLT according to the study-specific definition (see Table 1). No patient experienced any AE of grade 4 or 5. No SAE, serious adverse reaction, or suspected unexpected serious adverse reaction was reported. No patient terminated their study treatment prematurely or underwent dose reduction due to any treatment-related AE or for any other reason (e.g., tumor progression). Table 4 lists all documented AEs at a patient level. Table 5 summarizes AEs at a study level.

sec.p: Two patients developed grade 3 postoperative complication according to Clavien-Dindo classification: pneumonia in patient 2 and wound dehiscence plus postoperative anastomotic leakage in patient 5. The other three resected patients did not have any complications. The length of hospital stay ranged from 10 to 13 days, except for the patient 5, who required 37 days of inpatient treatment. Data on post-study treatment and long-term outcomes are not part of this analysis.

sec.title: Efficacy Results
sec.p: Two out of five resected patients achieved a minor response (TRG 3 according to the Becker scale), one patient showed a subtotal regression (TRG 1b), while two patients achieved a TRG 1a regression and pCR (ypT0 N0) [16]. R0 resection was accomplished in four out of the five resected patients, while one patient had an R1 resection. Table 6 summarizes the TNM stage before therapy and histopathological findings. In patient 5 with peritoneal carcinomatosis at restaging, peritoneal biopsies showed no HER2 expression (IHC 0). Both patients whose tumors were classified as Becker TRG 3 experienced Clavien-Dindo grade 3 postoperative complications [15]. One of the 2 patients underwent an R1 resection, developed an anastomotic leakage, and reassessment of the HER2 status in the resection specimen revealed absence of HER2 expression (IHC 0).

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report to evaluate the safety, feasibility, and preliminary antitumor activity of neoadjuvant T-DXd in combination with 5-FU and FA in western patients with resectable HER2-positive EGA. The neoadjuvant (preoperative) component of perioperative therapy for EGA is of critical importance, as only around 70% of patients initiate adjuvant (postoperative) treatment, and approximately half complete it [2, 4]. The histological response of the primary tumor and locoregional lymph nodes to systemic therapy correlates with survival outcomes and is frequently considered an early surrogate endpoint in neoadjuvant therapy trials [16]. The addition of HER2-directed antibodies to neoadjuvant therapy has shown to improve histological response, but studies published until today were underpowered or not designed to show increments in survival outcomes [6–8]. In the first-line metastatic setting, the ADC T-DXd in combination with ctx has demonstrated substantial efficacy, raising the question of its potential role in curative-intent settings [10]. However, resistance to HER2-targeted therapy attributable to intratumoral HER2 heterogeneity is a well-recognized phenomenon [17]. Additionally, the safety of combining an ADC such as T-DXd with ctx warrants careful evaluation. Therefore, the introduction of a HER2-targeted ADC like T-DXd should be rigorously investigated in a phase I/II trial. Our initial safety and activity evaluation of the NeoART safety run-in cohort suggests the feasibility of the concept and fosters optimism for positive study outcomes as the trial continues.

Notably, in the NeoART safety cohort, one patient was found to have previously undetected peritoneal carcinomatosis at the time of the planned resection, while another patient with only minor response underwent an R1 resection complicated by postoperative anastomotic leakage. In both cases, analyses of peritoneal carcinomatosis biopsies and the resection specimen, respectively, demonstrated absent HER2 expression, in contrast to the primary tumor biopsies, underscoring the challenges of spatial and temporal biomarker heterogeneity in EGA. Two of five resected patients in the safety cohort achieved a pCR. Both histopathologic response and negative lymph node status have been identified as favorable prognostic markers and have been proposed as potential criteria for omitting adjuvant therapy within multimodal treatment strategies, given the excellent prognosis and the lack of additional benefit observed in retrospective analyses [18, 19].

None of the findings warranted discontinuation of the trial or modification of the protocol. However, recent results from the MATTERHORN trial demonstrated a survival benefit with the addition of the PD-L1-directed antibody durvalumab to standard perioperative FLOT ctx (docetaxel, oxaliplatin, and 5-FU/FA) [4, 5]. Similarly, the KEYNOTE-811 trial showed a survival benefit in the first-line metastatic setting for HER2- and PD-L1-positive EGA with the addition of the programmed cell death 1 antibody pembrolizumab to trastuzumab in combination with platinum- and 5-FU-based ctx [20, 21]. Consequently, the NeoART protocol will be amended to include durvalumab.

In subsequent planned cohorts of the NeoART trial, the addition of oxaliplatin will also be evaluated. The decision to initiate treatment with T-DXd plus 5-FU/FA and without oxaliplatin was based on previously presented first-line data in HER2-positive advanced EGA demonstrating high response rates while aiming to avoid excessive toxicity [22]. It is important to emphasize that T-DXd should be regarded primarily as a targeted yet highly cytotoxic compound, associated with class-specific adverse events typical of topoisomerase I inhibitors, including hematologic and gastrointestinal toxicities. At the same time, its mechanism of action may help overcome HER2 heterogeneity, as demonstrated in breast cancer, where activity has been observed even in tumors with low HER2 expression, likely mediated by a bystander effect via its cleavable linker [23]. Therefore, the addition of another cytotoxic agent such as oxaliplatin warrants careful evaluation, for which the NeoART trial setting was specifically designed.
